pattern: Batch processing, change data capture and immutable storage
summary: Compare three ways a fictional subscription library delivers monthly content entitlements to a data lake.
scope: Illustrative architecture proposal for Larkspur Library. Includes diagrams, correction paths, audit trade-offs, a modeled cost comparison, operational safeguards, and open decisions. Volume and cost figures are study assumptions and estimates.

componentNotes.entitlement-job: Day 1: initial load (active as of cutoff). Then add new subscriptions daily through month-end. Skip 10 a.m.–2 p.m.
componentNotes.a-rundeck: Day 1: initial load (active as of cutoff). Then add new subscriptions daily through month-end. Skip 10 a.m.–2 p.m.
componentNotes.a-worker: Reads job state and resumes. Small batches + rate limits. Retries with backoff. Keeps PII out of logs.
componentNotes.a-registry: Replica or materialized view. subscriptions + plan_configs. ID, plan, status and dates only.
componentNotes.a-rules: Monthly categories and tiers. Study guides stack by tier (Gold = Bronze + Silver + Gold). Books use separate rules.
componentNotes.a-source: Transactional entitlements table. Items available to subscribers. Read-only, in small batches.
componentNotes.a-state: One run per reporting month. Pending / running / completed / failed. Cursor of the last batch.
componentNotes.a-cdc: Read-only user. Publishes this table only. Ignores the purge.
componentNotes.a-history: INSERT only (ON CONFLICT). Key: subscription + item + reporting month. Subscription ID only.
componentNotes.a-purge: DROP PARTITION for the old month (about 30 days). Wait for lake confirmation.
componentNotes.b-rundeck: Day 1: initial load (active as of cutoff). Then add new subscriptions daily through month-end. Skip 10 a.m.–2 p.m.
componentNotes.b-worker: Reads job state and resumes. Small batches + rate limits. Retries with backoff. Keeps PII out of logs.
componentNotes.b-registry: Replica or materialized view. subscriptions + plan_configs. ID, plan, status and dates only.
componentNotes.b-rules: Maps plans to tiers. Skips per-item expansion. Records the rule version. One row per subscription.
componentNotes.b-source: Transactional entitlements table. Items available to subscribers. Read-only, in small batches.
componentNotes.b-state: One run per reporting month. Pending / running / completed / failed. Cursor of the last batch.
componentNotes.b-cdc: Read-only user. Publishes these two tables. Ignores the purge.
componentNotes.b-lake: Joins both tables. Full history. Audit.
componentNotes.b-grants: One row per subscription. Plan, tier and period. Rule version · IDs only.
componentNotes.b-catalog: Tier + reporting month. Available catalog items. Immutable monthly snapshot. No personal data.
componentNotes.b-purge: DROP PARTITION for the old month (about 30 days). Wait for lake confirmation.
componentNotes.c-rundeck: Day 1: initial load (active as of cutoff). Then add new subscriptions daily through month-end. Skip 10 a.m.–2 p.m.
componentNotes.c-worker: Reads job state and resumes. Small batches + rate limits. Retries with backoff. Keeps PII out of logs.
componentNotes.c-registry: Replica or materialized view. subscriptions + plan_configs. ID, plan, status and dates only.
componentNotes.c-rules: Monthly categories and tiers. Study guides stack by tier (Gold = Bronze + Silver + Gold). Writes one file per batch.
componentNotes.c-source: Transactional entitlements table. Items available to subscribers. Read-only, in small batches.
componentNotes.c-state: One run per reporting month. Pending / running / completed / failed. Cursor of the last batch.
componentNotes.c-ingestion: Reads new files. Checks the manifest. No replication slot.
componentNotes.c-manifest: Files, row counts and hashes. Marks reporting month closed.
componentNotes.c-bucket: One Parquet file per batch. Stable key and retention lock. Subscription ID only. Create only if absent.
componentNotes.c-lifecycle: Bucket rule expires objects. No application DELETE.
componentNotes.compare-a:
Writes — One row per subscription × item
Storage — History Postgres
Lake ingestion — CDC
Builds the final list — Batch worker
Rows per month — ~4.7 billion
Cost at study scale — ~US$ 3,500 · R$ 19,400
Audit reproducibility — Partial (depends on source entitlements)
Corrections in-month — No correction path
WAL / slot risk — High
Purge — DROP PARTITION + verify CDC
Immediate lookup — Yes, 30 days in Postgres
Test effort — Low (table rows)
Fits baseline decision — Yes
Assumption — None
In one sentence — Precomputes the full list at high volume
Conclusion — Impractical at this scale
componentNotes.compare-b:
Writes — One row per subscription + monthly catalog
Storage — History Postgres
Lake ingestion — CDC from both tables
Builds the final list — Data lake joins both tables
Rows per month — ~158 million
Cost at study scale — ~US$ 230 · R$ 1,280
Audit reproducibility — Yes (saved snapshot)
Corrections in-month — New grant row
WAL / slot risk — Low
Purge — Same as A, with fewer rows
Immediate lookup — Yes, join both tables
Test effort — Low (table rows)
Fits baseline decision — Yes
Assumption — Access follows plan, tier and period
In one sentence — Stores grants and lets the lake join
Conclusion — Recommended
componentNotes.compare-c:
Writes — One Parquet file per batch
Storage — Bucket (Postgres tracks job state)
Lake ingestion — Data lake reads files without CDC
Builds the final list — Batch worker or data lake
Rows per month — Depends on file layout
Cost at study scale — ~US$ 260 (~US$ 25 at subscription grain)
Audit reproducibility — Partial (immutable files)
Corrections in-month — New versioned file
WAL / slot risk — None
Purge — Bucket lifecycle rule
Immediate lookup — After lake ingestion
Test effort — Medium (simulate a bucket)
Fits baseline decision — Reopens the decision
Assumption — Data lake supports file ingestion
In one sentence — Stores files under a retention lock
Conclusion — Alternative if the data team prefers files

componentNotes.execution-safeguards:
• Job state: prevent overlapping runs and time out orphaned running records
• Persist the cursor in the batch transaction
• C: derive the object key from the batch, then create only if absent
• Incremental runs replay a recent window. Set a fixed cutoff timezone
• Send failed subscriptions to an error table and continue the batch
• Rundeck: restrict triggers with ACLs, prevent concurrent runs, use Key Storage and omit PII
componentNotes.source-safeguards:
• Separate writer, purge and CDC privileges. Limit CDC to published tables
• A/B: set max_slot_wal_keep_size and alert on replication lag
• Entitlements Postgres: read-only access, keyset paging and small batches without a replica
• Registry: coordinate a replica or materialized view with the DBA. Avoid primary reads
• Registry view exposes ID, plan, status and dates. Exclude document IDs, email and phone
• Registry lacks a date index. Page by subscriptions.id and parallelize by ID range
• Registry holds current state. Snapshot at month-end. Order history lives in orders
componentNotes.retention-safeguards:
• Send a month-closed signal and per-run count to the lake
• LGPD: define lake retention and a data-subject deletion flow
componentNotes.proposed-design:
• B: use subscription-grain grants at the 158M-subscription study scale
• A: roughly 4.7 billion rows per month makes per-item materialization impractical
• C: consider files at subscription grain, matching B
• A registry replica or view introduces a DBA dependency for delivery
• At study scale, per-item expansion dominates modeled cost
componentNotes.questions:
• Can access be revoked? The answer governs corrections.
• Is the subscription ID sufficient? Product and engineering to confirm.
• Does the registry already feed the lake? The join could happen there.
• Can history share Entitlements Postgres? Who provisions it?
• Where should it run (Cloud Run Jobs, Kubernetes or a Rundeck node)?
• How does CDC handle DROP PARTITION and DELETE?
• Who owns the registry read replica or view, and what is the lead time?
• Can orders reconstruct effective dates for a closed month?
componentNotes.design-notes:
Proposal for review · Option A is the baseline after an engineering discussion · Redis was ruled out for this workflow's transactional needs · Scale assumption: 158 million active subscriptions
Subscription is the key · Monthly processing with daily backfill · No replica for Entitlements Postgres. Read it in small batches. Read the registry through a replica or materialized view because direct database access and an API are outside the source team's scope.
